items.body: Ah, NOX. Poor NOX. Alas, that's how it shook out. Or at least the end of GOG. It was not an especially close-run thing. And that's because it's truly weird one-of-a-kind. For those unlucky enough to have never had a Turkish kebab, it is a mixture of meat placed on a rotisserie, and a carver is used to cut it up into small strips. In the PC homage, there is a spinning fan, GPU, motherboard, and PSU inside a glass case, with four fans at the bottom and four fans at the top to control the temps. The pole in the center of the build has an RGB strip around it, illuminating all the hardware. It's a truly ridiculous build, and one I'd assume was purely for show, if the creator didn't also post it on builds.gg , a PC building website, to explain the methodology. items.title: الموعد والمدينة وهوية المنافس.. برشلونة يحدد تفاصيل ودية المغرب
items.summary: قبل الأهلي.. الفريق الكتالوني يصطدم بمنافس عربي جديد
items.body: قبل الأهلي.. الفريق الكتالوني يصطدم بمنافس عربي جديد رسم نادي برشلونة الخطوط العريضة للمباراة الودية التي سيخوضها في المغرب خلال الفترة المقبلة، قبل بداية الموسم الكروي الجديد 2026-2027. وكانت تقارير صحفية قد كشفت، في وقت سابق، عن رغبة برشلونة في إقامة مباراة ودية بالمغرب ، قبل أن تكشف صحيفة "سبورت" الكتالونية عن تفاصيل تلك المباراة. وأوضحت الصحيفة أن النادي الكتالوني يعمل في الوقت الحالي على إنهاء تفاصيل تلك المباراة، حيث ستُلعب في مدينة طنجة المغربية، يوم 15 أغسطس/آب المقبل. وأشارت الصحيفة إلى أن برشلونة استقر على أن تكون المباراة ضد أحد الأندية المغربية، لا سيما وأن الدوري المحلي لن ينطلق قبل شهر أكتوبر/تشرين الأول المقبل. وستكون تلك المباراة هي قبل الأخيرة التي يخوضها برشلونة، في إطار استعداداته للموسم الجديد، قبل أن يواجه الأهلي المصري، يوم 19 أغسطس/آب المقبل، على ملعب سبوتيفاي كامب نو، في بطولة كأس خوان جامبر الودية. ويخوض الفريق الكتالوني معسكرًا في إنجلترا خلال الوقت الحالي، سيختتمه بخوض مواجهتين وديتين أمام برمنجهام سيتي يوم 31 يوليو/تموز الجاري، وبريستون نورث إند يوم 3 أغسطس/آب المقبل. بعد ذلك، يتجه برشلونة إلى إيطاليا، يوم 8 أغسطس/آب المقبل، لخوض البطولة الثلاثية في أوديني، والتي يلتقي خلالها بنوتنجهام فورست الإنجليزي وأودينيزي الإيطالي، قبل وديتي المغرب والأهلي.

Despite continuing strong demand for memory from the AI industry, SK hynix has found itself missing investor expectations. Poor lamb. SK hynix was forecast to cross a slightly more face-melting profit threshold of 84 trillion won (about $58 billion) by the end of June. Analysts attribute the miss to a slowing of HBM4 shipments, with revenue from those to be recorded next quarter instead. To be clear, the 79.3 trillion the company actually made is far from disastrous, and still represents a 257% year-over-year boost to quarterly revenue . However, missing the revenue forecast has manifested in a share slump of about 9.6%. The stock itself has also halved in value (though that does mean it's still up by 115% so far this year). items.title: رفضه الرجاء.. موهوب مغربي يلحق بصيباري في الدوري الألماني
items.summary: هل ينجح في "البوندسليجا"؟
items.body: هل ينجح في "البوندسليجا"؟ اقترب لاعب مغربي جديد من الانتقال إلى الدوري الألماني خلال الموسم المقبل، بعدما رفض نادي الرجاء التعاقد معه في وقت سابق. وقال موقع "فوت ميركاتو" الفرنسي إن نادي أوجسبورج الألماني يرغب في التعاقد مع توفيق بن الطيب، مهاجم اتحاد التواركة المغربي، خلال فترة الانتقالات الصيفية الحالية. وأوضح الموقع أن النادي الألماني يعمل في الوقت الحالي على التفاوض مع نظيره المغربي، من أجل ضم بن الطيب بشكل رسمي، لا سيما بعد المستويات المميزة التي قدمها خلال الموسم الماضي. ولعب صاحب الـ24 عامًا في الموسم الماضي رفقة نادي تروا على سبيل الإعارة، ليحصل على لقب هداف دوري الدرجة الثانية الفرنسي برصيد 18 هدفًا. وقبل الانتقال إلى فرنسا، ارتبط اسم بن الطيب بنادي الرجاء في الميركاتو الصيفي الماضي، غير أن النادي المغربي رفض فكرة التعاقد معه. ورغم قصر قامته (180 سم)، فإن المهاجم المغربي قدم مستويات مميزة في جميع محطاته، ومن بينها نادي رودي الذي لعب له مُعارًا أيضًا في الموسم قبل الماضي، وسجل معه 10 أهداف في 29 مباراة بدوري الدرجة الثانية الفرنسي. يُذكر أن الدوري الألماني كان شاهدًا على حضور العديد من المواهب المغربية القوية، كان آخرها إسماعيل صيباري الذي تعاقد معه العملاق البافاري بايرن ميونخ خلال فترة الانتقالات الصيفية الحالية.

items.title: The latest ugly-cool immersive sim is scratching my itch for new Deus Ex
items.summary: And it lets you drive, which feels somehow momentous.
items.body: There's something defiant about the trend of deliberately ugly immersive sims. It is a statement: mechanics are king and beauty is a distraction, so here is something we scraped out of the vents on a PlayStation 1. I admire it. Not the graphics; the graphics look awful. I admire the sentiment. The latest in this proud tradition is Parkside: Decayed Soul Manipulation (in environments not restricted by the PC Gamer style guide, that title is rendered in all caps) from Banana Hardsoft, which releases on the 31st of July but has a demo you can play right now. It's got a System Shock start with a Deus Ex finish: you're Alexander, a hacker in a rundown world where the billboards blare messages like "Do Not Hinder Law Enforcement". You hack a little too deep and men with guns kick down your door. It's not System Shock's Trioptimum Corp, though, it's a gang of zealots set up like the Catholic Illuminati. They strap you into a machine that lets you remotely pilot a combat-ready body and send you off to kill a man. It's all part of the ineffable plan to serve the Divine Rod. Or something. items.body: الكرة المصرية على صفيح ساخن أشعل أحد الأئمة بوزارة الأوقاف المصرية حالة من الجدل خلال الساعات الأخيرة، بسبب السخرية من النادي الأهلي. وتداول رواد مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي مقطع فيديو لإمام يرتدي الزي الأزهري من أمام بوابة نادي الزمالك، سخر فيه من الغريم التقليدي الأهلي، بسبب فشله في التأهل للنسخة المقبلة من دوري أبطال أفريقيا. وأثار مقطع الفيديو حالة من الغضب بين رواد مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي، حيث اعتبروا أن هذا التصرف لا يليق بالزي الأزهري الذي كان يرتديه الإمام خلال حديثه. وأصدرت وزارة الأوقاف بيانًا عبر حسابها الرسمي على موقع "فيسبوك"، أعلنت فيه فتح تحقيق عاجل بشأن مقطع الفيديو المُنتشر. وأوضحت الوزارة أنها ستتخذ الإجراءات المناسبة، من أجل صون الصورة العامة لها، ولرسالة الإمام، ولوقار الزي الأزهري، حيث أشارت إلى أنه تحدث في شأن غير دعوي، وبأسلوب انطوى على السخرية. وكان الأهلي قد تأهل لبطولة الكونفدرالية الأفريقية، عقب الحصول على المركز الثالث في جدول ترتيب الدوري المصري خلال الموسم الماضي، فيما تأهل ناديا الزمالك وبيراميدز إلى دوري الأبطال.

items.title: Keychron's gaming mouse firmware is going open-source, while the company critiques 'firmware you can't read, can't audit, can't change'
items.summary: I'm always in favour of more open-source software.
items.body: Keychron, the gaming peripheral creator, has developed a name for itself as a defender of open-source software over the last few years. It has an entire ' Open Source Design Project ', where it posts access to files to customise its keyboards, and it even uses ZMK and QMK, which are open-source software for keyboards. Open-source mouse firmware has gone unloved by the company, until now. Keychron announced on X that it's currently developing ZGM, an open-source gaming mouse software for use with its mice. The company plans to launch ZGM at the start of 2027. Keychron says in the announcement, "Every gaming mouse on the market runs firmware you can't read, can't audit, can't change. So we built it ourselves." Alongside this, the company has published a new website , explaining the benefits of open-source gaming mouse firmware and how it came about. The new software is built on Zephyr ROTS and designed to be scalable and modular, meaning it can support multiple hardware variants and can work with unique sensors, buttons, and scroll wheels without rewriting. items.title: Cooler Master V8 Ace 3DHP review
items.summary: Proving air coolers are still cool in 2026.
items.body: It's not often we see serious innovation in air cooling; many merely spin on tried and tested formulae. That's not the case here, however, as the Cooler Master V8 Ace 3DHP is offering something new to PC builders: 3DHP technology. I first glimpsed the 3DHP (3D Heat Pipe) tech in a backroom of Cooler Master's Taipei HQ in 2025. I was under a strict oath not to talk about anything I saw in that room, which was easy enough, as it was almost empty except for a pair of air coolers: one using a traditional U-shape heatpipe design and the other using 3DHP. The 3DHP design includes an additional heatpipe at the centre of the U-shape. The benefit of this extra heatpipe is clear through a thermal imaging camera: there's no deadzone (cool patch) in the middle of the cooler. For the V8 Ace, in particular, 3DHP is used on two of its six heatpipes—the two big ones in the middle—with the other four in a more traditional layout. Altogether, there are a lot of heatpipes running through every part of this single-tower cooler. That's the thing to remember when looking over the results from my testing with the V8 Ace 3DHP below. items.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation boss has been thinking about ways to make a mysterious boss suitable for the upcoming crossover raid with Final Fantasy 14
items.summary: "Nobody wants to go in there and just see Cloud looking like Cloud, but massive."
items.body: I'm surprised it's taken 13 years to happen, but Final Fantasy 14 is finally bringing Final Fantasy 7 to the MMO in a big way. Upcoming expansion Evercold is getting an entire raid series dedicated to the remake trilogy—that's 12 whole fights spread across three tiers which will trickle in over the course of Evercold's two-to-three year lifespan. It's been a long wait, but as Rebirth and Revelation director Naoki Hamaguchi tells me, the stars finally aligned to make the crossover happen. "I was speaking to [FF14 director and producer Naoki Yoshida] about the fact that Evercold and Revelation release dates were actually going to end up being fairly close together," he said. "And so, instead of having them as two separate things … let's do something that can really energise the Final Fantasy franchise as a whole." As for what we can expect when the raid series lands? Well, that's all very mysterious right now. Hamaguchi kept tight-lipped on what sort of fights we'll see, though he did hint towards efforts being made to make a Final Fantasy 7 boss more suitable for Final Fantasy 14's raids. items.body: Final Fantasy 14 may be an MMO, but it's certainly never sacrificed the series' talent for excellent storytelling. It's stuffed with incredible worldbuilding, a cherished cast of characters, and heart-wrenching story beats that'll get players shedding a tear from just hearing a few notes from a song that played during a cutscene. It is, however, also a story that requires hundreds of hours to experience the full breadth of its narrative—spread across A Realm Reborn and five meaty expansions, with a sixth one on the way. While Square Enix has pruned quests here and there in an attempt to streamline the experience, it's still a helluva lot of game to ask a new player to commit to. I've had the good fortune to be playing since the beginning, but I can say with absolute certainty that if I was only just starting the game, I'd be damn near paralysed by how daunting the new player experience is— especially if you want to play with friends who are already across the finish line. items.body: Subnautica 2 might be a chill survival game, but the journey to May's early access launch was filled with drama, legal battles and accusations of sabotage. Just recalling it all is giving me a massive headache, which I'm now going to give to you. In 2025, Krafton ousted Unknown World's leadership and delayed Subnautica 2's early access launch. The publisher accused the studio heads of abandoning the game , who then fired back and accused Krafton of delaying Subnautica 2 so it wouldn't have to pay a promised $250 million earnout —a strategy Krafton's CEO came up with thanks to ChatGPT . The result of the dispute was a judge forcing Krafton to reinstate Unknown Worlds CEO Ted Gill and extend the earnout period . But the drama wasn't over. Krafton then almost immediately announced an imminent early access release date, which Gill believed was its final attempt to sabotage the game and avoid paying what was promised. It's genuinely a miracle that after all of this Subnautica 2 launched and it was really, really good. Earlier this month, it hit a new milestone: 5 million copies sold . items.title: Linux kernel patch can boost the Steam Deck's 1% low frame rate by as much as 31% in early testing
items.summary: There's life in the old handheld yet.
items.body: A number of recent Linux driver patches has reportedly resulted in significant performance gains for the Steam Deck . Valve's handheld runs on the Linux-based SteamOS, and these patches can apparently improve the Steam Deck's 1% low frame rates by as much as 31%. A fresh 'epp_boost' feature for the AMD P-State driver is largely responsible for the performance boost. David Vernet, a Linux kernel hacker at Meta, is the developer behind it. The feature implements per-core Energy Performance Preference (EPP) for AMD CPUs. As far as I know, it's not yet been reviewed by AMD's Linux kernel engineers, though Vernet explains via the Linux kernel mailing list that it was developed with gaming specifically in mind (via Phoronix ). Vernet offers a technical breakdown of the inefficiency these patches are designed to address, writing, "In active (EPP) mode the platform autonomously picks the operating point between min_perf and max_perf, biased by the EPP hint, and the kernel only rewrites the CPPC request on policy or limit changes. items.body: Sony won't be producing game disks anymore—a decision that's been met industry-wide with a mixture of frustration and ambivalence , depending on which side of the fence you fall on. Personally, I don't think a videogame company or distribution platform having final say over whether you concretely own something is healthy, even if I am admittedly arm-deep in Steam purchases. It's a controversial enough mandate that it even got a french politician riled up ! It's also something that makes the creators of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 a little melancholy, per a recent interview with Automaton : "Personally, I find it super sad because I really like video game stores," says CEO and Creative Director of Sandfall Interactive Guillaume Broche. items.title: Microsoft reportedly using TPM chips to weed out Windows piracy
items.summary: Spare a thought for the system administrators.
items.body: Microsoft's Trusted Platform Module, specifically TPM 2.0, has been part of Windows 11's system requirements since the operating system's introduction in 2021 . Now that the TPM is ubiquitous, being included with most CPUs for many years, Microsoft is looking to leverage it "to activate Windows devices at scale." Currently, the enterprise sector activates Windows via Microsoft's Key Management Service (KMS), but according to the Windows IT Pro Blog , "modern organizations increasingly require stronger assurances around device identity and activation integrity." Basically, hackers can already clone or fake KMS server software, so the TPM is intended to provide a hardware-level security check to curb this. The blog post then very briefly breaks down how TPM attestation works. Essentially, the KMS host flashes its TPM credentials to prove its hardware identity. These TPM credentials also reveal whether the KMS host has been tampered with or not, and Microsoft checks these before it allows the host to activate any devices. It takes a complicated lithographic machine to produce a modern chip, and there are two main types: EUV (Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography) and DUV (Deep Ultraviolet Lithography). It's the older of the two, DUV, that a Chinese company is said to have figured out. After stealing from one esports hotel alone, Li allegedly recruited Cheng, and the two stayed at different hotels from May 15 to May 31, dismantling PCs as they went. The pair reportedly listed the memory on a second-hand trading platform, and allegedly made a profit of 13,200 yuan (just shy of $2,000) from 16 sticks total. Memory could further become a target for theft as it's light and easy to conceal, and with AI sucking it all up, its prices have continued to rise over the last few years. Arguably, it offers the best gram/cost ratio out of any part of a PC right now.
